environment: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200; Intel Core i5-12400F; 12 logical processors; NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 SUPER; .NET 10.0.11; Release builds (Square NativeAOT via -r win-x64 -p:PublishAot=true)
workload: 900x1240 client viewport; three groups of 240 boxes: transform (translate/rotate/scale), opacity, width; 6s linear loops; sequential 30s measurements after warmup
windowGeometry: All three targets start with their OS window (outer frame) at screen (100, 100). Square and Avalonia: 916x1279 outer / 900x1240 client. Chrome: 916x1391 outer / 900x1240 CSS viewport at devicePixelRatio 1, no scrolling.
cpuDefinition: Process CPU time divided by measured wall time, expressed as a percentage of one logical processor. Chrome samples its dedicated browser process tree. Whole-machine percentages divide by 12.
memoryDefinition: Private memory = process-private committed bytes; working set = resident bytes (summing Chrome children can double-count shared pages). Mean and observed peak from approximately 1 Hz samples across the measurement window, in MiB. These figures do not include dedicated GPU VRAM.
limitations: Square runs its own animation timeline and submits frames from a Win32 timer loop; its FPS is render submissions, not scanout. Avalonia and Chrome FPS count animation-frame callbacks, so the three FPS numbers are throughput indicators measured on different clocks.

Square's Direct2D backend was measured with SQUARE_DIRECT2D_REQUIRE_HARDWARE=1 (hardware device). GPU engine utilization and dedicated VRAM were not sampled, so the higher private/working memory of the Direct2D runs includes device and swap-chain resources without a GPU-side breakdown.

Chrome was measured with chrome-devtools-mcp attached to its isolated profile (--user-data-dir=...\.cache\chrome-devtools-mcp\chrome-profile); DevTools attachment adds overhead on top of a plain interactive session. Its CPU/memory follow 8 initially live processes; a child spawned later would not be included and exited children retain their last CPU sample. The FPS and process-metric intervals were started within approximately one second of each other.

All windows were placed at screen (100, 100) before measuring so occlusion and composition conditions match; the Chrome outer window is taller because of browser UI, while its CSS viewport matches the 900x1240 client area of the other two targets.
